title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Reference, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade & Rollback
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This reference document consolidates deployment guidance for Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem), common reference architectures, packaging and airgap options, day-2 operational runbooks, and a prescriptive upgrade and rollback procedure. It is intended for solutions engineers, SREs, and customer engineering teams executing production deployments or responsible for ongoing operations.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: VPC-hosted Private control plane, customer VPC peering, and fully on-prem / airgapped deployments (customer-managed network, KMS integration, and GPU hosts).
- Audience: deployment engineers, SRE, customer infra teams, solutions engineering.

High-level architecture (summary):
- Control plane (Redwood-managed / customer-hosted depending on contract) communicates with a private data plane in the customer VPC or on-prem cluster.
- Components typically installed in customer environment: inference runtime (GPU nodes), orchestration agents, metrics and tracing collectors, log forwarders, and optional model cache layer.
- Integration points: KMS/HSM for key management, private container registry or airgap bundle, monitoring exporter endpoints, and optional NFS/MinIO for model artifacts.

Prerequisites checklist (network, security, compute):
1) Network & identity
   - VPCs: dedicated subnets for control-plane agents, inference pools, and management services.
   - Security groups / firewalls: allow outbound-only to Redwood control endpoints (if using Redwood-managed control plane) or allow inbound from Redwood ops IPs for support tunnels only.
   - DNS: internal DNS entries for service discovery; ensure *.redwood-internal DNS mapping or /etc/hosts for airgap installs.
   - Service accounts: customer-provided IAM roles with least-privilege for storage, logging, and metrics.

2) Compute & storage
   - GPU nodes: recommended families: NVIDIA A10/A100 series; GPU driver CUDA >= 12.0 recommended.
   - Node sizing: baseline 8 GPUs per node for high-throughput inference pools, smaller nodes (1-2 GPUs) for latency-sensitive workloads.
   - Persistent storage: s3-compatible object store for model artifacts (MinIO supported), and ephemeral NVMe for KV cache.

3) Security & compliance
   - KMS: customer KMS or HSM integration required for encryption-at-rest of model keys.
   - Audit logging: forward pod/container audit logs to customer SIEM; configure retention per compliance.
   - RBAC: map Redwood roles to customer identity providers (OIDC/LDAP) for operator access.

Reference architectures (short descriptions and when to use):
- VPC-managed (recommended for most customers):
  - Description: Redwood Private control plane deployed into customer VPC with private endpoints. Easier lifecycle, integrates with customer cloud networking and KMS.
  - Use cases: cloud-first customers requiring data residency with minimal on-prem complexity.
  - Diagram (text): Control plane (private subnets) <-> Inference GPU pool (private subnets) -- MinIO/S3 

- On-prem airgapped:
  - Description: Full bundle (airgap tarball) plus on-prem control plane and image registry. Designed for regulated customers with no outbound connectivity.
  - Use cases: regulated financial, government, or high-security environments.
  - Packaging: OCI images in tar bundle, Helm charts, preflight validator script, offline license and license server.

- Hybrid (cloud control plane + on-prem inference pool):
  - Description: Control plane hosted in a customer-approved cloud region or Redwood-managed but connected through secure egress; inference runs on-prem GPUs.
  - Use cases: customers who want central management but keep inference physically isolated or close to data.

On-prem packaging and delivery options:
- Standard install: Helm charts + public container registry (requires outbound to registry.redwood.ai).
- Airgap bundle: tar.gz containing all OCI images, Helm charts, Kubernetes CRDs, and offline installer. Includes a preflight.sh that verifies node drivers, kernel versions, and available disk/GPU memory.
- Appliance image: for strict airgap customers we provide a validated VM image with preinstalled runtime and drivers.

Packaging checklist (airgap):
- Signed bundle checksum (sha256).
- All container images exported as oci images/registry format.
- Offline installer binary and installer docs included.
- License file and activation mechanism.
- Preflight validator with a generated report.

Preflight validation (example checks):
- Kernel driver >= 520 (NVIDIA), CUDA toolkit presence, nvidia-smi output OK.
- Helm client >= 3.8, kubectl >= 1.25.
- Nodes report correct GPU types and counts.
- Disk IO and network latency within thresholds.

Day-2 operations (runbooks and common tasks):
- Observability and alerts
  - Ensure Prometheus exporters (node-exporter, nvidia-smi exporter) and Grafana dashboards are deployed.
  - Standard alerts: GPU memory pressure (>85% per GPU), inference latency SLO breaches (p99 > target), model load failures.
- Scaling
  - Horizontal: Add additional GPU nodes to the inference pool and label them with redwood.inference/gpu-pool=<pool-name>.
  - Vertical: Adjust per-node GPU allocation using runtime config and restart agent (see runbook).
- Routine ops: log rotation, certificate renewal, secrets rotation (KMS key rotation), and model cache invalidation.
- Backup/restore
  - Backup: nightly snapshot of model metadata DB and critical configs to S3-compatible bucket; retain per policy.
  - Restore: documented steps to restore metadata first, then warm model cache.

Upgrade and rollback procedure (prescriptive):
- Goals: zero-data-loss, minimal latency impact, safe rollback within defined window.
- Preconditions (must pass before upgrade):
  1) Current health checks green for >24 hours.
  2) Backups complete and checksum verified (metadata DB backup + model artifact manifests).
  3) Canary pool available with at least 2 GPU nodes for testing.

- Upgrade steps (summary):
  1) Create a release branch and tag; publish airgap bundle or update Helm repo.
  2) Apply control-plane schema migrations in maintenance mode (if any).
  3) Deploy to canary pool: helm upgrade --install redwood-runtime --namespace redwood-canary -f values-canary.yaml ./chart
  4) Run functional smoke tests against canary (sample tests: generation latency < target, model accuracy sanity checks, KV cache warm-up).
  5) Monitor for 2x expected p50/p95 latencies, error rates < 0.1% for 30 minutes.
  6) If tests pass, progressively roll out to additional pools using rolling update strategy (maxUnavailable=1 per node pool).
  7) Post-upgrade validation: run validation suite, compare model outputs on canonical prompts, check telemetry and billing metrics.

- Rollback triggers:
- Immediate rollback if any of:
  - Error rate increase > 1% absolute or >5x baseline.
  - p99 latency degradation outside SLO for >15 minutes.
  - Model correctness regression flagged by eval harness.

- Rollback procedure (fast path):
  1) Pause rollout (helm rollout pause / deployment).
  2) Rollback to previous chart: helm rollback redwood-runtime <previous_release_rev> --namespace <ns>.
  3) Reapply traffic shaping (route traffic away from affected nodes) and validate.
  4) If metadata migration ran and is incompatible, trigger metadata restore from pre-upgrade backup: run restore script with --from-backup <backup_id>.

- Post-rollback actions: incident review, capture heap/dump logs from failed revision, quarantined images for postmortem.

Customer requirements library (template & examples):
- Network requirements (template):
  - Required outbound: control-plane endpoints list (or none for airgap).
  - IP ranges and ports: 10.0.0.0/16 internal, allow TCP 443 outbound to registry endpoints, ports 2379 for etcd (if self-hosted), 9090 for prometheus scraping (restrict to monitoring subnet).
- Compute requirements (template):
  - Minimum GPU type: NVIDIA A10 or equivalent.
  - Node OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS preferred, kernel >= 5.15.
  - Disk: 200GB ephemeral NVMe per GPU for KV cache.
- Compliance & security requirements (template):
  - KMS integration: customer-managed KMS with key rotation policy 90 days.
  - Audit logs retention: 365 days (default for regulated customers).
- Example customer profile (high-level):
  - Customer A (finance): 8 A100 nodes, airgap, dedicated on-prem NFS, HSM for key storage, full audit retention.
  - Customer B (healthcare): VPC deployment, MinIO object store, OIDC SSO, daily backups to encrypted S3 bucket.

Operational runbooks (quick links and excerpts):
- Model load failure: check model manifest, object storage access, node GPU readiness, agent logs (/var/log/redwood/agent.log).
- High p99 latency: check GPU utilization, batching configuration, network contention, and recent config changes.
- Node replacement: cordon node, drain workloads (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets), replace hardware, ensure nvidia drivers, uncordon.

SLOs and operational thresholds (recommended defaults):
- Inference latency SLOs: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 120ms, p99 < 250ms (depends on model/sequence length).
- Availability SLO: 99.9% (rolling monthly).
- Error budget handling: automated alerting at 10% burn in 24h, paging at 25% burn.

Ownership, contacts, and escalation:
- Private Deployments Product Owner: Marco Li (product@redwood.ai).
- Deployment Engineering team (primary): eng-private-deployments@redwood.ai.
- Escalation: follow internal escalation playbook -> oncall SRE -> Deployment Eng lead.

Appendix A - Example helm values snippet (text YAML):
replicaCount: 3
image:
  repository: registry.redwood.internal/redwood-runtime
  tag: v2026.02.1
resources:
  limits:
    nvidia.com/gpu: 1
nodeSelector:
  redwood-inference/gpu: "true"
affinity: {}

Appendix B - Sample commands (non-airgap):
- Install: helm repo add redwood https://helm.redwood.ai/charts && helm install redwood-runtime redwood/redwood-runtime -f values.yaml --namespace redwood
- Check GPU nodes: kubectl get nodes -l redwood-inference/gpu -o wide
- Run canary smoke tests: ./tools/smoke-tests/run_smoke.sh --endpoint https://canary.redwood.local --model gpt-small

Appendix C - Preflight script exit codes summary:
- 0: pass
- 1: fatal mismatch (stop install)
- 2: warning (manual review required)
